title: High-resolution and Deep Phylogenetic Reconstruction of Ancestral States from Large Transcriptomic Data Sets
author: Sumanth Kumar Mutte
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Create BLAST databases
steps.instruction: For each transcriptome and proteome, build a BLAST database using makeblastdb. Use ‘-dbtype nucl’ for transcriptome FASTA files and ‘-dbtype prot’ for proteome FASTA files.

steps.title: Prepare query FASTA file
steps.instruction: Assemble a FASTA file of protein sequences from well‑annotated genomes covering diverse taxa (list provided in Appendix‑1). This file will be used as the BLAST query.

steps.title: Run BLAST searches
steps.instruction: Search the query file against the transcriptome database with tblastn and against the proteome database with blastp. Keep all default parameters, set the E‑value cutoff to 0.01, and output results in tab‑delimited format (outfmt 6).

substeps.instruction: tblastn -query filename.fa -db transcriptome.fasta -out output.blast -evalue 0.01 -outfmt '6 qseqid sseqid slen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore score length pident nident positive ppos mismatch gaps frames qcovs qcovhsp sseq'

blastp -query filename.fa -db proteome.fasta -out output.blast -evalue 0.01 -outfmt '6 qseqid sseqid slen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore score length pident nident positive ppos mismatch gaps frames qcovs qcovhsp sseq'

steps.title: Extract subject IDs
steps.instruction: From each BLAST output file, pull the second column (subject identifiers), sort them, and remove duplicates, writing the list to SubjectIdentifiers.txt.

steps.title: Retrieve selected sequences
steps.instruction: Using the list of identifiers, extract the matching transcript or protein records from the original FASTA files with faSomeRecords.

steps.title: Translate transcripts to proteins
steps.instruction: Identify long open reading frames (≥100 aa) in the selected transcripts with TransDecoder.LongOrfs, then predict coding sequences and translate them with TransDecoder.Predict.

steps.title: Align sequences with MAFFT
steps.instruction: Align the protein (or translated) sequences using MAFFT with the globalpair algorithm and 1000 iterative refinements.

steps.title: Trim alignment with trimAl
steps.instruction: Remove poorly aligned columns using trimAl. Apply a gap‑threshold of 0.2 (remove positions with ≥80 % gaps) as a default; adjust to 0.3–0.4 for moderately conserved domains or 0.6–0.8 for highly conserved proteins. Optionally discard sequences shorter than ¼ of the average length in JalView.

steps.title: Select evolutionary model
steps.instruction: Determine the best substitution model for each cleaned alignment. Use ModelFinder (built‑in IQ‑TREE) for automatic selection, or run ModelTest‑NG or PartitionFinder when ModelFinder disagrees with ModelTest‑NG.

steps.title: Construct phylogenetic trees
steps.instruction: Build maximum‑likelihood trees using IQ‑TREE, RAxML, and optionally PhyML. Use 1,000 rapid bootstraps and 1,000 SH‑aLRT replicates in IQ‑TREE; in RAxML employ rapid bootstrapping with autoMRE stopping, a random seed (‑x 12345 ‑p 12345), and the model from the previous step; in PhyML run 100 bootstraps with empirical amino‑acid frequencies and SPR tree search.

substeps.instruction: raxmlHPC-PTHREADS-AVX2 -f a -x 12345 -p 12345 -j -# autoMRE -m PROTGAMMAJTT -s CleanAlignment.fa -n OutputName
PhyML-3.1_linux64 -i CleanAlignment.fa -d aa -b 100 -m JTT -f e -s SPR -a e

steps.title: Visualize and curate trees
steps.instruction: Upload the resulting trees to the iTOL web server, add protein‑domain information (InterProScan or MEME), sequence lengths (TransDecoder), and taxonomic data (OneKP/MMETSP). Manually inspect trees, removing branches caused by long‑branch attraction, partial sequences, or misplaced taxa; if many problematic branches remain, repeat the analysis with additional species or after discarding spurious sequences.
